title: Storm Rachel Gets Weaker but Brings More Rain
summary:
A storm named Rachel caused flooding and damage in Southern California over the weekend. On Sunday, the National Weather Service said Rachel had become weaker. It is now called a post-tropical storm. It can still bring heavy rain and wind.

The storm moved inland across the desert Southwest. The weather service warned of flash floods. Big waves kept hitting towns on the coast.

In beach cities like Long Beach and Newport Beach, waves broke through sand walls built to hold back the ocean. Some homes near the water were partly underwater. Las Vegas broke a rainfall record for one day. Utah, including Salt Lake City, was told to watch for floods.

Forecasters think Rachel may be a sign of more storms. They expect the strongest El Niño on record this winter. El Niño is when parts of the Pacific Ocean get warmer than usual, which can change the weather.

California is getting ready. The state is setting out more than 4 million sandbags and checking its dams.
why_it_matters: Knowing about storms and floods helps families get ready and stay safe.
